hot.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
hot.summary: A speculative decoding framework named DSpark integrates semi-autoregressive generation with confidence-scheduled verification to enhance Large Language Model inference efficiency. It significantly improves per-user generation speeds and aggregate throughput in live production environments by dynamically optimizing draft quality and resource allocation.

hot.title: PhysisForcing: Physics Reinforced World Simulator for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: PhysisForcing, a framework developed by Peking University and NVIDIA, enhances the physical consistency of generated videos for robotic manipulation by reinforcing hierarchical physics supervision in interaction-critical regions. The method improved average success rates on RoboTwin 2.0 tasks from 68.2% to 72.8% and achieved a 9.2% performance gain on the R-Bench benchmark.

hot.title: Qwen-Image-2.0-RL Technical Report
hot.summary: The Qwen-Image-2.0-RL framework improves the Qwen-Image-2.0 diffusion model's visual quality and instruction-following by integrating reinforcement learning from human feedback and on-policy distillation. This approach achieved a +2.61 improvement on the Qwen-Image-Bench for text-to-image generation and a +78 Elo rating increase in human preference for text-to-image tasks.

hot.title: Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data
hot.summary: Autodata introduces an agentic framework for autonomously generating and curating high-quality synthetic data to train large language models (LLMs). Through iterative feedback and meta-optimization of the data generation process, it produces data that optimally challenges target models, leading to performance improvements of up to 13.2% in CS research tasks and 17.0% in legal reasoning tasks, while enhancing reasoning efficiency in mathematical problems.

hot.title: Ask, Don't Judge: Binary Questions for Interpretable LLM Evaluation and Self-Improvement
hot.summary: The BINEVAL framework offers an interpretable approach to evaluating large language model outputs by decomposing quality assessment into atomic binary questions, providing fine-grained feedback and natural-language explanations. This method improved evaluation accuracy, achieving higher correlations with human judgments across summarization and dialogue tasks, and enabled iterative prompt optimization for both evaluators and generators.

hot.title: Towards Automating Scientific Review with Google's Paper Assistant Tool
hot.summary: Google Research developed the Paper Assistant Tool (PAT), an agentic AI framework designed for in-depth scientific manuscript review, to address the escalating validation bottleneck in academic publishing. The tool demonstrated 89.7% error detection accuracy on a filtered benchmark of retracted math/CS papers and was rated by over 90% of authors as helpful in improving clarity and identifying substantive errors in pilot programs.

hot.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
hot.summary: Researchers at the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI) developed Orca, a general world foundation model built on a "Next-State-Prediction" paradigm, which learns a unified latent representation of world states from multimodal signals. This approach improves performance across diverse downstream tasks including text generation, interaction-conditioned image prediction, and real-robot action generation, demonstrating scalability with increased model and data size.

hot.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
hot.summary: This research systematically evaluates existing large language model agent memory systems from a data management perspective, introducing a four-module analytical framework and conducting extensive empirical studies across 12 architectures and five benchmark workloads. The study provides insights into architectural trade-offs, operational costs, and how different memory components impact task effectiveness, retrieval fidelity, and dynamic update robustness.

hot.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent
hot.summary: The Agents-A1 project by Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introduces a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that attains performance levels comparable to trillion-parameter models on long-horizon tasks by emphasizing agentic horizon scaling. The model notably outperformed 1T-parameter models on benchmarks like SEAL-0 (56.4) and IFBench (80.6) and demonstrated gold-medal-level results in a 12-hour machine learning optimization task.

hot.title: SimFoundry: Modular and Automated Scene Generation for Policy Learning and Evaluation
hot.summary: SimFoundry presents a modular, automated system for generating interactive, sim-ready scenes and diverse training environments from a single video, facilitating robot policy evaluation and training. The system achieved a mean Pearson correlation of 0.911 for real-to-sim evaluations and demonstrated up to 50 percentage points improvement in sim-to-real transfer success with object variations.

hot.title: DanceOPD: On-Policy Generative Field Distillation
hot.summary: DanceOPD is an on-policy generative field distillation framework that enables a single flow-matching model to effectively compose diverse capabilities like text-to-image generation and various image editing tasks. The framework consistently improves target capabilities, such as editing scores by up to 21.9% in specific categories, while preserving or enhancing anchor generation quality by up to 2.0% in T2I metrics.

hot.title: Accelerating Gemini Nano models on Pixel with frozen Multi-Token Prediction
LA4VLA: Learning to Act without Seeing via Language-Action Pretraining
hot.summary: Researchers developed LA4VLA, a framework for pretraining robot manipulation policies by decoupling language-action learning from visual inputs. This approach, utilizing the LA-33K dataset of vision-agnostic action episodes, improves downstream task success rates, enhances robustness to visual perturbations, and strengthens language-action grounding in VLA models.

hot.title: Translation as a Bridging Action: Transferring Manipulation Skills from Humans to Robots
hot.summary: Researchers from HKU-MMLab and ByteDance Seed developed a robotic manipulation framework that transfers skills from human demonstrations using a relative wrist translation as a "bridging action". This method enabled robots to learn novel manipulation tasks with a 0.57 success rate and improved data efficiency for few-shot robot post-training, outperforming approaches based on 6DoF human wrist actions.

hot.title: Domain-Informed Multi-View Self-Distillation for Astronomical Light-Curve Representation Learning with JEPA
OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: OPID (On-Policy Skill Distillation) introduces a framework that enhances large language model (LLM) agents by extracting hierarchical, natural-language skills directly from their completed on-policy trajectories. This method consistently improves agent performance across embodied reasoning, web navigation, and search-based QA tasks, demonstrating up to a 26.5 point increase in success rate on WebShop for smaller LLMs and better sample efficiency compared to outcome-only reinforcement learning.

hot.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search
hot.summary: Xia et al. investigate "context rot," the degradation of LLM agent capabilities with increasing context length in multi-turn, multi-source deep search tasks. The study systematically diagnoses this phenomenon using a novel error taxonomy and evaluates various context management and rot-aware rejection sampling strategies, finding that a combined "Keep Latest with summarization" method provides an optimal balance for mitigation and significantly improves reliability.

hot.title: ScaleAware-JEPA: Latent Representation for Discovery in Multiscale Physical Fields
Hallucination in World Models is Predictable and Preventable
hot.summary: Researchers at UC San Diego reframe hallucination in visual world models as a data coverage issue, developing three model-internal signals that predict hallucination with a robust negative Spearman correlation of approximately -0.80. Their work introduces the MMBench2 dataset and demonstrates that coverage-aware training and targeted data collection can prevent hallucination, improving downstream Model Predictive Control performance on unseen tasks by adapting models with as few as 50 trajectories.

hot.title: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Researchers at Renmin University of China and ByteDance developed iLLaDA, an 8-billion parameter fully bidirectional masked diffusion language model, achieving performance competitive with leading autoregressive models and substantial improvements over prior diffusion LLMs across various benchmarks.

likes.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
likes.summary: Qwen-AgentWorld introduces a family of language world models (LWMs) that simulate diverse agentic environments, surpassing frontier LLMs on the AgentWorldBench and improving agent performance across various downstream tasks. These models enhance agent learning through scalable, controllable simulation and by integrating internal predictive reasoning for action refinement.

likes.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
likes.summary: This research systematically investigates and establishes an open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic language models, identifying effective strategies for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data and demonstrating its efficacy with a new dataset that improves agentic model performance. The study also explores reinforcement learning (RL) data curation, finding that specific RL data sources can induce exploratory agent behaviors and further enhance capabilities when combined with SFT.

likes.title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: This research introduces the World Value Model (WVM), which repurposes spatiotemporal priors from video world models to achieve a generalist robotic value estimator with enhanced temporal understanding. It establishes a new evaluation benchmark, Suboptimal-Value-Bench, demonstrating WVM's superior ability to track task progress in suboptimal scenarios and guide robust policy learning from mixed-quality data.

InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
likes.summary: INSIGHT introduces a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to autonomously acquire new manipulation skills by identifying missing primitive actions and generating their own training data. The system enables robots to continually expand their learned skill vocabulary, achieving high success rates in novel tasks while retaining prior capabilities and improving execution efficiency.

likes.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers?
likes.summary: This work introduces NatureBench, a benchmark and automated pipeline (NatureGym), to evaluate AI coding agents' ability to surpass published scientific state-of-the-art (SOTA) across 90 tasks derived from Nature-family papers. It finds that current frontier agents achieve limited SOTA surpassing (max 17.8% of tasks) and moderate SOTA matching (max 47.8%), relying primarily on generic ML engineering rather than novel scientific discovery.

likes.title: Qwen-Image-Agent: Bridging the Context Gap in Real-World Image Generation
likes.summary: The Qwen-Image-Agent, a training-free framework from the Alibaba Group, addresses the "Context Gap" in real-world image generation by actively constructing a comprehensive generation context from incomplete user input. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on the newly proposed IA-Bench benchmark, as well as WISE-Verified and MindBench, significantly improving upon direct generation models by integrating planning, reasoning, search, memory, and feedback capabilities.

likes.title: Fast LeWorldModel
likes.summary: Fast-LeWM introduces an action-prefix prediction method for visual world models, enabling parallel forecasting of future latent states. This approach achieves a 3.9x acceleration in dynamics evaluation and a 48% reduction in total planning time while improving planning success rates to 90.5% on average and mitigating error accumulation in long-horizon predictions.

likes.title: Improving Neural Network Training by Decoupling the Magnitude and Direction of Weight Vectors
likes.summary: Researchers at EPFL's Machine Learning and Optimization Lab developed Magnitude–Direction (MD) Decoupling, an optimizer modification that separates the learning dynamics of weight vector magnitudes and directions. This approach consistently improved performance, eliminated the need for weight decay and learning rate warmup, facilitated learning rate transfer across model sizes, and reduced compute requirements by approximately 2x for large Mixture-of-Experts models.

likes.title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
likes.summary: JAXBench introduces a TPU-native benchmark suite to evaluate autonomous kernel optimization methods, featuring 50 JAX workloads derived from production LLMs and providing device-side profiling for accurate measurement. The benchmark demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLM agents can achieve a 1.36x geomean speedup over XLA compilation, reaching about 77% of hand-tuned Pallas kernel performance on specific compute-bound tasks.
